title: The 2048 ceiling
words: Show that even perfect play almost never reaches the theoretical top tile in 2048.
math: Prove $\Pr(\text{reach }131072)<10^{-6}$ for every strategy on the $4\times4$ board with standard random spawns.

title: Emirps are infinite
words: Show infinitely many primes become a different prime when reversed.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $\operatorname{rev}(p)\neq p$ prime.

title: Gomoku on hats
words: Prove the first player wins five-in-a-row on an infinite board of hat tiles.
math: Prove the first player has a winning strategy in the 5-in-a-row game on the hat adjacency graph (rows = geodesic paths).

title: Ladder in a corridor
words: What is the smallest area of floor needed to move a ladder of length 1 around a corner?
math: Determine the minimal area of a region inside the width-$w$ right-angled corridor in which a unit segment can be moved from one arm to the other.

title: Lopsided prime gaps
words: Show there are infinitely many places where a prime gap is bigger than a power of the gap right before it.
math: Prove $p_{n+1}-p_n>(p_n-p_{n-1})^{1.01}$ for infinitely many $n$.

title: Readable Riemann
words: The 2026 Riemann proof is a giant machine-checked archive. Write a proof people can read.
math: Give a proof of the Riemann hypothesis of at most 100 pages acceptable to expert referees.

title: Explicit Navier–Stokes blow-up
words: Write down a forced Navier–Stokes blow-up as an explicit formula instead of a computer-assisted construction.
math: Give closed-form smooth $u_0,f$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ for which the Navier–Stokes solution blows up in finite time.

title: XY model on hats
words: Rotating magnets on a hat tiling should show the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition.
math: Prove a BKT transition (power-law correlations at low $T$, exponential at high $T$) for the XY model on the hat graph.

title: Prime Nim with prime-power moves
words: Allow subtracting any prime power. Find exactly which piles lose.
math: Characterize the P-positions of the subtraction game with move set $\{p^k: p\text{ prime},k\ge1\}$.

title: Hat-tiled Sudoku
words: Fill a 49-tile hat patch with digits so every neighbourhood of seven touching tiles has all digits. Count the fillings.
math: Count proper "hat Sudoku" fillings of the canonical 49-tile cluster where each designated 7-tile block is a permutation of $\{1..7\}$.

title: Largest-factor cycles
words: Find every loop of the largest-factor Collatz map.
math: Prove every periodic orbit of $f(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(3n+1)$ (odd) lies in an explicit finite list, and give it.

title: Shuffle with a cut
words: Do a perfect shuffle, then cut k cards from top to bottom, and repeat. How many repetitions bring the deck back?
math: For the permutation $c_k\circ\sigma_{\text{out}}$ on $2n$ cards, determine its order as a function of $n$ and $k$.

title: Hyperbolic lonely runners
words: Runners move along closed paths on a hyperbolic surface. Show one eventually gets far from all others.
math: For geodesic flows on a closed hyperbolic surface along $n$ distinct primitive closed geodesics, prove a uniform separation time exists, with optimal bound.

title: Shortest proof that √2 is irrational
words: Find the shortest possible Lean proof that the square root of 2 is irrational, and prove nothing shorter works.
math: Over Lean 4 core tactics on top of Mathlib's definitions, find the minimal tactic-step proof of `Irrational (Real.sqrt 2)` and certify minimality.

title: Fast Prime Nim
words: Compute Prime Nim values up to a trillion.
math: Give an algorithm computing $G(n)$ for all $n\le10^{12}$ in time $o(N^{1.5})$ and run it.

title: Hat aperiodicity in Lean, minimal
words: Give a computer-checked proof that the hat tiles only aperiodically, in under 2000 lines.
math: Produce a Lean 4 proof of the hat's aperiodicity of at most 2000 lines using only Mathlib.

title: Reverse-square cycles
words: Square and reverse the digits, repeatedly. Show there are infinitely many different loops.
math: Prove $R(n)=\operatorname{rev}(n^2)$ has infinitely many distinct cycles.

title: Undecidable polykite tiling
words: For sets of five shapes made of kites, deciding whether they tile the plane is unsolvable by any algorithm.
math: Prove that tileability of $\mathbb{R}^2$ by finite sets of at most 5 polykites is undecidable.

title: Smoke-free corridor
words: Show a corridor's smoke clears in a predictable time when air flows through it.
math: For advection–diffusion in a periodic corridor with Stokes flow, find the sharp exponential decay rate of a passive scalar in terms of geometry.

title: Largest-factor Collatz for all n
words: Prove every start reaches a loop under the largest-factor Collatz map.
math: Prove every orbit of $f(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(3n+1)$ (odd) is eventually periodic.

title: Hyperbolic firefighter budgets
words: In a hyperbolic tiling, fire spreads exponentially, so no fixed crew stops it. How fast must the crew grow?
math: On the $\{7,3\}$ tiling graph, find the minimal growth of budgets $k_t$ (firefighters at turn $t$) that contains any single fire.

title: Doubled-twin residues
words: Call p a "doubled twin" if p and p + 2 are twin primes and their doubles plus one, 2p + 1 and 2p + 3, are twin primes too. Show such p must sit in specific residue classes.
math: If $p>7$ and $p,\,p+2,\,2p+1,\,2p+3$ are all prime, prove $p\equiv 29 \pmod{30}$ and $p\equiv 1,4,6 \pmod 7$.

title: Prime Nim growth
words: Show the Prime Nim values grow, but slowly.
math: Prove $G(n)\le Cn/\log n$ for the Grundy function of the prime subtraction game.

title: Two-to-one Keller maps
words: Known Jacobian counterexamples cover most points three or more times. Is there one covering most points exactly twice?
math: Decide whether some $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ has generic fiber size exactly 2.

title: Billiards in the sofa
words: A ball bounces inside Gerver's sofa shape. Find its shortest closed bouncing path.
math: Determine the minimal-length periodic billiard trajectory in Gerver's sofa and prove minimality.

title: Unit-distance barrier
words: Show the 2026 number-field method for many equal distances can never reach exponent 1.1.
math: Prove every construction of the Alon–Bloom–Gowers–…–Sawin type (lattices from number fields of bounded class-field degree) gives $u(n)\le n^{1.1}$.

title: Cops on square sums
words: How many cops catch a robber moving along square-sum links?
math: Determine $c(S_N)$, the cop number of the square-sum graph, for all large $N$.

title: Graceful path forests
words: Label the vertices of a forest made of separate paths with distinct numbers so that the differences along edges are all different.
math: For a forest of paths with $m$ edges and $c$ components, find a bijection $\ell:V\to\{0,\dots,m+c-1\}$ with all $|\ell(u)-\ell(v)|$, $uv\in E$, distinct.

title: Blokus Duo
words: Who wins two-player Blokus with perfect play?
math: Weakly solve Blokus Duo on the $14\times14$ board with standard starting points.

title: Hard-hat transition
words: Show the gas of non-overlapping hats freezes abruptly at some density.
math: Prove the hard-hat lattice gas has a first-order phase transition in the activity.

title: Optimal 3D origami
words: For every 3D shape, find the smallest sheet of paper that folds into it.
math: Give a characterization, with an algorithm, of the minimal-area square that folds into any given polyhedral surface.

title: Wang tile busy beaver
words: Using eight colored tile types that cannot tile the whole plane, how big a square can they still tile?
math: Over sets of 8 Wang tiles that do not tile $\mathbb{Z}^2$, determine the maximum $n$ such that the $n\times n$ square is tileable.

title: Fire on a cylinder
words: A fire burns on a grid wrapped into an infinite tube of width n. How many firefighters per turn stop it?
math: On $C_n\times\mathbb{Z}$ with 4-neighbour spread, find the least $k(n)$ that always contains a single fire, for every $n$.

title: Graceful trees up to 50 vertices in Lean
words: Give a computer-checked proof that every tree with up to 50 vertices is graceful.
math: Formalize in Lean 4 that all trees on $\le50$ vertices admit graceful labelings.

title: No prism sofa
words: Show the best 3D sofa is genuinely three-dimensional, not just a flat shape extruded upward.
math: Prove no optimal solid for the $1\times1$ square corridor is of the form $A\times[0,1]$.

title: Prime Langford pairings
words: Arrange two copies each of 1 to n so the two copies of k sit exactly the k-th prime apart. For which n is this possible?
math: Determine all $n$ for which $1,1,\dots,n,n$ can be arranged so the two copies of $k$ are $p_k$ positions apart.

title: The sofa's boundary is not algebraic
words: Gerver's sofa is bounded by 18 curve pieces. Show some of them are not polynomial curves.
math: Prove at least one boundary arc of Gerver's sofa is not contained in any algebraic curve.

title: Largest-factor Collatz stopping time
words: How many steps does the largest-factor Collatz map take, on average, to reach 1?
math: Prove $\frac1x\sum_{n\le x}T(n)\sim c\log x$ for the stopping time $T$ of $f$, and compute $c$.

title: Voice leading in 31-tone
words: Find the shortest path through all chords of 31-tone equal temperament where each move changes one note by one step.
math: Determine the minimal Hamiltonian path length in the voice-leading graph of 4-note chords in $\mathbb{Z}_{31}$.

title: Counting minimal Sudokus
words: How many uniquely solvable Sudokus with no removable clue exist, as the board grows?
math: Find the asymptotics of the number of minimal uniquely solvable $n^2\times n^2$ puzzles.

title: Geodesic squares on surfaces
words: Every smooth closed curve on a convex surface should pass through the corners of a square made of shortest paths.
math: Prove every smooth simple closed curve on a smooth convex surface inscribes a geodesic quadrilateral with equal sides and equal diagonals.

title: Toroidal Hex
words: Hex on a doughnut: the board wraps around, and you win with a chain that loops the long way. Who wins on 7 × 7?
math: On the $7\times7$ Hex board with opposite sides identified, a player wins with a non-contractible chain of their colour; determine the winner and whether draws occur.

title: Hard hats
words: Hat-shaped particles that cannot overlap form a gas. Show it behaves simply when sparse.
math: For the hard-core lattice gas of hats on the hat tiling hull, prove uniqueness of the Gibbs measure at activity $z<z_0$ for explicit $z_0$.

title: Voice-leading geodesics
words: The space of chords is an orbifold. Find its shortest closed loops that pass through every chord type.
math: In the orbifold $\mathbb{T}^3/S_3$ of 3-note chords, find the shortest closed geodesic meeting every $\mathbb{Z}_{12}$-chord orbit.

title: Certified plane coloring
words: If the plane needs seven colors, a finite set of points proves it. Find the smallest such set and check it by computer.
math: If $\chi(\mathbb{R}^2)=7$, find a minimal 7-chromatic finite unit-distance graph and certify it in Lean.

title: Seven-free twin primes
words: Show there are infinitely many twin primes with no digit 7 in either.
math: Prove infinitely many $p$ with $p,p+2$ prime and both 7-free in base 10.

title: Self-avoiding walks on the hat tiling
words: Count paths across hat tiles that never revisit a tile, and show their growth rate is new.
math: Prove the connective constant $\mu_{\text{hat}}$ exists for the hat adjacency graph and $\mu_{\text{hat}}\ne\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}$.

title: Two colors for square sums, avoiding triangles
words: Show every way to 2-color 1 to N, for large N, makes three same-colored numbers whose pairwise sums are all squares.
math: Prove for large $N$ every 2-coloring of $[N]$ has a monochromatic triangle in $S_N$.

title: Polykite tiling undecidability
words: Show there's no algorithm that decides whether a finite set of polykites tiles the plane.
math: Prove the tiling problem for finite sets of polykites (edges on the kite grid) is undecidable.

title: Perfect Minesweeper
words: What is the exact chance that perfect play wins expert Minesweeper?
math: Compute $\sup_\sigma\Pr(\text{win})$ for $30\times16$ with 99 uniform mines and a safe first click.

title: 3D Ising on the spectre stack
words: Stack spectre tilings in layers and find the critical temperature exactly.
math: Compute $\beta_c$ for the Ising model on $\text{spectre}\times\mathbb{Z}$.

title: Largest-factor Collatz heights
words: For almost every start, the largest-factor Collatz orbit never climbs past a fixed power of where it started.
math: Prove there is $C$ with $\max_k f^k(n)\le n^C$ for a density-1 set of $n$.

title: Prime necklace
words: Arrange 1 to N in a circle so neighbours add to a prime, but numbers two apart add to a composite.
math: Prove that for all $N\ge50$ there is a cyclic order of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ with $x_i+x_{i+1}$ prime and $x_i+x_{i+2}$ composite for all $i$.

title: Shuffle orders are unbounded below
words: Show some three-pile shuffles take only a tiny number of repeats to return the deck, infinitely often.
math: Prove $\operatorname{ord}(\sigma_n)\le n^{0.1}$ for infinitely many $n$.

title: Hyperbolic square peg
words: Every closed curve in the hyperbolic plane should pass through the corners of some hyperbolic square.
math: Prove every Jordan curve in $\mathbb{H}^2$ contains the four vertices of a regular hyperbolic quadrilateral.

title: Integer Keller collisions
words: Show any Jacobian-conjecture counterexample must send two different integer points to the same place.
math: Prove every non-invertible Keller map in $\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\dots,x_n]^n$ is non-injective on $\mathbb{Z}^n$.

title: Cube-sum colors
words: Join numbers that add up to a perfect cube. Show a fixed number of colors always suffices.
math: For $C_N$ with $a\sim b\iff a+b$ a cube, prove $\sup_N\chi(C_N)<\infty$ and find it.

title: Penrose firefighter
words: Fire spreads along a Penrose tiling's edges. How many firefighters per turn can trap any fire?
math: On the vertex graph of a Penrose rhomb tiling, find the least $k$ such that protecting $k$ vertices per turn contains a fire from any single vertex.

title: Sofa for every angle
words: Find the optimal sofa for a hallway turning by any angle, not just 90°.
math: For every $\theta\in(0,\pi)$, determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor turning by $\theta$.

title: Independent prime-gap formalization
words: Check the 2026 record that prime gaps of at most 186 occur forever, with a fresh computer proof written independently.
math: Give an independent Lean 4 proof of $\liminf_{n}(p_{n+1}-p_n)\le186$.

title: Effective Riemann constants
words: Extract explicit, usable prime-counting error bounds from the 2026 Riemann proof.
math: From the 2026 Lean proof, extract and formally verify $|\pi(x)-\operatorname{li}(x)|\le\frac{1}{8\pi}\sqrt{x}\log x$ for all $x\ge2657$.

title: Firebreak with wind
words: How long must a firebreak be to save a round town from a wind-driven fire?
math: For front speed $a+b\cos\theta$ and a disc town at distance $D$, find the minimal length of a curve built at speed $\sigma$ that protects the town.

title: Funnel sofa
words: The corridor narrows after the corner from width 1 to width 1/2. Find the best Hammersley-style sofa.
math: Over shapes of the form (quarter-disc, rectangle, quarter-disc) minus a half-disc, maximize area for turning from a width-1 arm into a width-$\tfrac12$ arm.

title: Firefighters on the front line
words: Firefighters may only protect cells touching the fire. How many per turn are needed now?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with protected cells required to be 4-adjacent to the burned set, find the least per-turn number containing a single fire.

title: Hat mixing time
words: Randomly flip local patches of a hat tiling. Show it mixes in polynomial time.
math: For local-move Glauber dynamics on hat tilings of an $L\times L$ region, prove mixing time $L^{O(1)}$.

title: Graceful forests
words: Every forest should admit a labeling where all edge differences are distinct. For a single tree this is the graceful tree conjecture.
math: Prove every forest with $m$ edges and $c$ components has a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+c-1\}$ with distinct edge differences.

title: Random graceful forests
words: Almost every random forest has the distinct-edge-difference labeling.
math: For a uniform random forest with $m$ edges and $c\sim\alpha m$ components, prove the graceful-forest labeling exists with probability $\to1$.

title: Poincaré in Lean
words: Turn Perelman's proof of the Poincaré conjecture into a computer-checked proof.
math: Formalize in Lean 4: every closed simply connected 3-manifold is homeomorphic to $S^3$.

title: Squared squares with consecutive primes
words: Find a perfect squared square whose square sides are consecutive primes.
math: Find or rule out a perfect squared square whose component sides are $p_k,p_{k+1},\dots,p_{k+r}$ for some $k,r$.

title: Seven-free primes have a bounded gap
words: Show infinitely many pairs of seven-free primes lie within a fixed distance of each other.
math: Prove $\liminf(q_{n+1}-q_n)<\infty$ where $q_n$ enumerates the 7-free primes.

title: Ambidextrous 3D sofa
words: Find the largest solid that can turn either left or right at the end of a square pipe.
math: Maximize volume over solids admissible for both the left and right turns of the $1\times1$ corridor.

title: Kepler, compressed
words: Make the computer-checked proof of the densest sphere packing far shorter.
math: Give a Lean 4 proof of the Kepler conjecture in under 100,000 lines.

title: Chen with no sevens
words: Show infinitely many seven-free primes p have p + 2 a product of at most two seven-free primes.
math: Prove infinitely many 7-free primes $p$ with $p+2=q_1q_2$ or $q_1$, all $q_i$ prime and 7-free.

title: Square-sum chromatic number
words: Find exactly how many colors the infinite square-sum graph needs.
math: Determine $\chi(S_\infty)$ exactly.

title: S-tetromino squares
words: For which square sizes can you tile the square with S-shaped tetrominoes plus a single 1 × 1 piece?
math: Determine all $n$ for which an $n\times n$ square admits a tiling by copies of the S-tetromino (rotations and reflections allowed) and one monomino.

title: Square-sum pancyclicity
words: Show the square-sum graph has cycles of every possible length.
math: Prove $S_N$ is pancyclic on its 2-connected core for all large $N$.

title: Infinitely many prime squared squares
words: Show there are infinitely many perfect squared squares whose pieces all have prime sides.
math: Prove infinitely many perfect squared squares with all component sides prime.

title: Seven-free prime count
words: Count primes avoiding the digit 7 with a much sharper error term.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x:\ 7\notin p\}=\kappa\,\#\{n\le x: 7\notin n\}/\log x\,(1+O(x^{-\delta}))$ with explicit $\delta>0$.

title: Hex on hats
words: Play Hex on a board made of hat tiles. Can games end in a draw, and who wins on a small board?
math: For Hex on hat-tiled rhombus boards, decide whether draws are possible, and solve side length 5.

title: Smallest non-Rupert solid
words: Some solids can pass a copy of themselves through a hole in themselves. Find the simplest convex solid that cannot.
math: Find the minimum number of vertices of a convex polyhedron $P$ without Rupert's property, and an extremal example.

title: Sudoku count asymptotics
words: Count n²×n² Sudoku grids exactly, to leading order.
math: Prove $\#\text{Sudoku}(n)=\left(\frac{(n^2)!^{2}}{n^{2n^2}e^{\dots}}\right)\!(1+o(1))$ with an explicit leading term.

title: Weyl algebra endomorphism
words: The Jacobian counterexamples imply a non-surjective symmetry of a noncommutative algebra. Write one down.
math: Give an explicit non-surjective endomorphism of the Weyl algebra $A_2(\mathbb{C})$.

title: Wythoff Prime Nim
words: With two piles, remove a prime from one pile or the same prime from both. Describe the losing positions.
math: Characterize the P-positions of the two-pile game with moves $(a,b)\to(a-p,b),(a,b-p),(a-p,b-p)$, $p$ prime.

title: Spectral gap of the spectre
words: Find the exact gaps in the energy levels of an electron moving on a spectre tiling.
math: Prove the spectrum of the adjacency operator on the spectre tiling has gaps labelled by an explicit $K$-theory group, with every label open.

title: Hat contact process
words: An infection spreads between neighbouring hat tiles and heals at random. Bound the critical infection rate tightly.
math: For the contact process on the hat graph, prove $\lambda_c$ lies in an explicit interval of relative width $\le 2\%$.

title: Sudoku transversals
words: In every completed big Sudoku, find a set of cells with one in each row, each column and each symbol.
math: Prove every $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku grid, viewed as a Latin square, has a transversal.

title: QCD in Lean
words: Check the 2026 rigorous construction of QCD with an independent computer proof.
math: Independently formalize the existence of 4D QCD satisfying the Osterwalder–Schrader axioms.

title: A four-dimensional einstein
words: Find one 4D shape that fills 4D space but only without repeating.
math: Find a connected tile $T\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ that tiles $\mathbb{R}^4$ by isometries but admits no periodic tiling.

title: Kissing number of the spectre
words: How many spectres can touch one central spectre without overlapping?
math: Determine the kissing number of the spectre polygon under rigid motions (reflections allowed).

title: Pulsating fire fronts
words: A fire spreads through a forest with regularly repeating fuel patches and steady wind. Show it moves at a well-defined average speed, and find the formula.
math: For $u_t=\Delta u+w\cdot\nabla u+f(x,u)$ with $f$ periodic in $x$ and KPP type, prove existence of pulsating fronts in every direction and give a variational formula for $c^*(e,w)$.

title: Doubled-twin asymptotic
words: Count the doubled-twin quadruples up to x exactly, to leading order.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: p,p+2,2p+1,2p+3\text{ prime}\}\sim\mathfrak{S}x/\log^4x$.

title: Seven-free Goldbach
words: Show almost every even number is a sum of two primes that have no digit 7.
math: Prove all but $o(x)$ even $n\le x$ are sums of two 7-free primes.

title: Aperiodic polykite census
words: The "hat" is made of 8 kites and tiles the plane only non-periodically. Find every such shape made of at most 12 kites.
math: Enumerate all polykites with $\le12$ kites (from the $\{6,3\}$ kite grid) that tile $\mathbb{R}^2$ but admit no periodic tiling.

title: Seven-free Sophie Germain
words: Show infinitely many primes p have 2p + 1 prime with no digit 7.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $2p+1$ prime and free of digit 7.

title: Lean golf is NP-hard
words: Show that finding the shortest proof using only a few basic Lean tactics is computationally hard.
math: Prove NP-hardness of: given a Lean 4 goal and $k$ in unary, is there a proof using only intro, apply, exact, rfl with at most $k$ steps?

title: Ringel for forests
words: Split a complete graph on 2m + 1 vertices into identical copies of any given forest with m edges.
math: Prove $K_{2m+1}$ decomposes into $2m+1$ copies of any forest with $m$ edges.

title: Random walks on square sums
words: How long does a random walk on the square-sum graph take to forget its starting point?
math: Determine the mixing time of simple random walk on the giant component of $S_N$ up to constants.

title: Keller maps in every dimension
words: Find the smallest dimension and degree where a Jacobian-conjecture counterexample exists, and list them all there.
math: Determine $\min\{(n,d)\}$ (lexicographic) such that a non-invertible Keller map $\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}^n$ of degree $d$ exists, and classify those.

title: Gerver constant is transcendental
words: Show the area of Gerver's sofa is not a root of any polynomial with integer coefficients.
math: Prove $\mu_G\approx2.2195$ is transcendental.

title: Keller maps with integer fibers
words: Show no Jacobian-conjecture counterexample with integer coefficients is injective on integer points but not invertible.
math: Prove every Keller map $F\in\mathbb{Z}[x,y,z]^3$ injective on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ is a polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^3$.
